text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 10 in history:
955 - King Otto I of Germany defeated the Magyars (Hungarians) at the Battle of Lechfeld, ending a threatened Magyar invasion.
1557 - The French army lost over 14,000 men when they tried to block a Spanish army under Count Egmont at the Battle of Saint Quentin in the Spanish-French Wars. The Spaniards lost just 50.
**1627 - France's Cardinal Richelieu began the siege of the Huguenot fortress at La Rochelle with royal troops. The fortress finally fell 14 months later in October 1628.

**1675 - The foundation stone of the Royal Observatory was laid at Greenwich in south London by order of King Charles II, to improve knowledge of the positions of stars and thus aid navigation. John Flamsteed became the first Astronomer Royal.
**1792 - King Louis XVI of France was arrested after a mob stormed the Tuileries in Paris and massacred the Swiss Guard, and the monarchy was suspended.

1810 - Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, born. Premier of Piedmont (1852) under Victor Emmanuel II, he modernised the duchy and was a key figure in the unification of Italy. He became its first prime minister in 1860.
1821 - The state of Missouri was admitted to the Union as the 24th of the United States.
1846 - In the United States, the Smithsonian Institution was established in Washington as a centre for scientific research from funds left at the bequest of British scientist James Smithson.
1865 - Aleksandr Konstantinovich Glazunov, Russian symphonic composer, born. He wrote eight completed symphonies and two piano concertos. One of his last works (1934) was a concerto for saxophone.
1874 - Herbert Hoover born. Statesman and 31st president of the U.S. from 1929-1933.
1885 - The first commercially operated electrical streetcar began operation in Baltimore in the United States.
1894 - Varahagiri Venkata Giri, Indian statesman, born. Prominent in India's Labour movement, he became minister of labour in 1937 and 1952. He was president of India from 1969-1974.
1895 - The first Promenade concert under conductor Henry Wood took place at Queen's Hall in London. He remained in sole charge of the "Proms", the annual British classical music festival, until 1940.
1904 - The Russian Fleet took heavy losses when the Japanese fleet blocked them as they were trying to escape from Port Arthur in the battle of the Yellow Sea, part of the Russian-Japanese War.
1913 - The Treaty of Bucharest was signed between Bulgaria and the Balkan allies Greece, Serbia, Montenegro and Romania, ending the second Balkan war.
1920 - The Treaty of Sevres was signed between Turkey and the Allied powers after World War One, relieving Turkey of much of the land ruled by the Ottoman Empire.
1928 - Eddie Fisher, U.S. singer and actor, born. He was married to Debbie Reynolds and later Elizabeth Taylor, with whom he made "Butterfield 8".
1944 - After three weeks of fighting, U.S. forces finally overran Pati Point and recaptured Guam from the Japanese in World War Two.
1964 - Pope Paul VI issued his first encyclical, "Ecclesiam Suam", which stated his willingness to mediate in international disputes.
**1966 - Orbiter 1 was launched from Cape Kennedy and became the first spacecraft to transmit Lunar photographs of possible landing sites. It crashed into the far side of the moon on October 29.
1995 - Former army buddies Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols were indicted for the devastating Oklahoma City bombing on April 19 that killed 168 people.
